Description-only: question formulation, source criticism and substantial historical research in the American Century. It is historical inquiry, not a dedicated political-science or Dutch/global-politics project.

alternatives.label: Global politics, governance and political economy
alternatives.concept: A programme investigating power, political regimes, international institutions and global political economy through comparative politics, political theory, international relations, law and economics. Quantitative and qualitative inquiry, policy analysis and historical study support evidence-based political argument. It offers broader study and does not reproduce the dedicated VU political-research projects or final thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual disciplinary study and specific contributions sustain the bounded concept; no Dutch specialist sequence, full political-science training or identical thesis is claimed.
progression: All covered offerings/formal earlier prerequisites checked against unchanged current workbook. PPD is in year one; statistical and law foundations precede dependents.

alternatives.label: International security, law and global governance
alternatives.concept: A programme studying international conflict, security and governance through peace/conflict inquiry, international and human-rights law, warfare and empire, radicalisation prevention and empirical methods. Data analysis and institutional research complement the political core. Historical work remains explicitly historical and does not become a dedicated global-politics thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual disciplinary study and specific contributions sustain the bounded concept; no Dutch specialist sequence, full political-science training or identical thesis is claimed.
progression: All covered offerings/formal earlier prerequisites checked against unchanged current workbook. PPD is in year one; statistical and law foundations precede dependents.
alternatives.distinctness: Six substantive substitutions shift from additional micro/public economics, rhetoric and persuasion toward warfare, criminal justice, radicalisation, empirical data and historical research, sustaining a different security/law emphasis.

candidates.label: International security, law and global governance
Political writing, debate and public argument
candidates.reason: Actual rhetoric, persuasion, PPD and policy memos already supply substantial writing/debate work in the closest programme. Stylistics and film/media courses were tested as further contributions, but broad audiovisual/US-media interpretation does not establish a new global-political communication specialism from these two academic-skill interests. No media-career or illustrative technology-company question is promoted into a new generator.

routeSelection.basis: Registry resolution case rc-0074 (normalization status step2-resolved-split) explicitly identifies cp-000112 as the English-taught 'Global Politics' track/version of the shared VU Political Science registration, distinct from the Dutch 'Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' track (cp-000113); the registry's own targets metadata records {"language":"ENG","focus":"global politics"} for this exact target. OER Article 10.2 confirms that, starting cohort 2025-2026, the bachelor's programme (RIO 56606) offers exactly two named tracks -- 'Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' (Dutch) and 'Political Science: Global Politics' (English) -- so the normalized target itself names this exact official route (Section 2.1 rule 1), confirmed by current official evidence for the 2026-2027 academic year and by the English-language 'political-science-global-politics' curriculum, future and admissions webpages themselves.

selection.assessment: Two independently assessed feasible, meaningfully distinct programmes pass for the confirmed core. A communication candidate is separately tested and does not establish enough additional global-political substance beyond the existing rhetorical/policy work; no third slot is manufactured.

blocks: Both examine political thought and normative political arguments; particular thinkers and sequences differ.
Both directly compare political regimes and institutions; UCR includes parties, electoral systems, state structures and democratisation.
Both examine European institutions in wider political contexts; UCR focuses on integration, decision-making and policy processes rather than an identical global-order syllabus.
Both study international relations and conflict/cooperation; UCR develops theory-guided cases and a UN negotiation simulation.
Both address international security and conflict. UCR develops conflict/peace theories and cases; a complete dedicated security-studies sequence is not implied.
Both develop empirical research design; UCR applies measurement, surveys, sampling and statistical analysis in a broader social-science setting.
Both develop qualitative inquiry; UCR provides actual interviews, coding and reflexivity without certifying identical political methods.

notes.text: UCR offers broader political, legal, economic and empirical inquiry. It does not reproduce the two dedicated VU political research projects, the full political-methods sequence or the required final political-science thesis. The security option combines actual conflict, law, warfare and radicalisation inquiry; it is not equivalent specialist security training.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Politics studies political power, international conflict and cooperation, global governance, comparative regimes and political economy, with quantitative and qualitative research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed global politics and empirical-methods core supports two meaningful broader UCR responses, while the revised-cohort final-year theory and research culmination remains outside the assessed scope. UCR supplies sustained political/institutional and empirical study with the option-specific emphases shown. Dedicated VU projects and the final thesis are not reproduced; a complete external progression pathway is not certified.

curriculum.limitation: The nominal degree is 180 EC. The confirmed first two years and 30 EC open study account for 150 EC. The compulsory final 30 EC allocation and third-year mentorship for 2026 entrants are not verified. The general 90 non-elective programme-EC thesis-entry rule, including the two academic-skills courses, is verified.
